transition_detector.reason: No authoritative addendum .docx exists. This skeleton is RECONSTRUCTED from an executed LOI, so there is nothing byte-exact to cross-check against. Pointing the detector at Powder Springs would validate the manifest against the document it was derived from - a tautology, not a check.
transition_detector.exit_condition: Per Claude Code: print the disabled state visibly on every run, and FAIL if a skeleton has the detector disabled while an authoritative template file for it exists. Disabled must not quietly become permanent.

_README: PROVISIONAL addendum skeleton for the Starbucks Contingency Addendum. Second skeleton,
appended after the letter skeleton, ALWAYS-EMITTING - no gating, no applies_when.
Its own index space, 0-based, independent of the letter manifest.
v2 CHANGES after Claude Code's review of v1:
- Headings re-keyed from `primary` to the new `heading` category. The loaded bodies do NOT
include their headings, so heading paragraphs have nothing behind them. The letter
paras 229-235 pattern does not transfer - that is ONE body whose body_text spans several
paragraphs, not two paragraphs sharing a body.
- idx 0 re-keyed from `instruction` to `heading`. As `instruction` it would never emit and
the addendum would ship with no title, though both sends carry one. Caught by Claude Code.
- other_contingency/main is now claimed by NOTHING and must stay in _unjoined_bodies.
NEW CATEGORY `heading`: emitted, carries no canonical body, rule-2 exempt exactly as
`letter_shell` is. Headings are TEMPLATE-OWNED - they never vary by deal and are supplied by
the skeleton, not by a body. This matches the letter convention where ~90 of 98 bodies
exclude their heading.
WHY PROVISIONAL: there is no addendum .docx. Built from Powder Springs, the less-edited of
the two sends. Douglasville is an edited copy and diverges in four places (below), so neither
send is authoritative and Powder Springs is only the better reconstruction base.
DIVERGENCES between the two sends, all resolved in favour of Powder Springs:
1. Preamble (idx 2)    - present in Powder Springs, DELETED in Douglasville.
2. Recorded Documents  - PS: '...Document to Starbucks approval to be recorded on ___.'
DGV: '...Document subject to Starbucks approval.' (no date at all)
3. Third-party approv. - PS keeps the '[from _________]' bracket; DGV removes it.
4. Exhibit C           - PS uses an en dash, DGV a hyphen. (Outside this skeleton's range.)
Divergence 1 is informative rather than a conflict: the preamble is a sample-language
INSTRUCTION, so a dealmaker deleting it is correct behaviour.
SCOPE ends at idx 16 - Claude Code reviewed and did not veto. The exhibit block that follows
(A/B/C/G/L/N/R/S plus the Landlord Workletter) is ATTACHMENT machinery, already modelled by
loi_attachment_requirement. Modelling it as skeleton paragraphs would add ~40 paragraphs that
rule 2 cannot check and rule 4 does not touch.
UNJOINED - companion change required, do not land this alone:
OUT of _unjoined_bodies (they now have paragraphs):
title_contingency/main, recorded_documents/main, third_party_approvals/main
STAYS OUT of any manifest, so STAYS IN _unjoined_bodies:
other_contingency/main - opt-in single free-text param; Powder Springs did not use it, so
no content paragraph exists in the reconstruction to claim it. Revisit when a send that
DOES use Other Contingency becomes available.
ALSO OUT when it gets its letter-skeleton paragraph:
future_construction/main - rides with this work without being part of it, easy to forget.
Final allowlist should be THREE entries, not two:
sale_of_property/main, early_termination/placeholder, other_contingency/main
ALLOWLIST ENTRIES ARE NOT ALL THE SAME KIND - worth distinguishing in the schema so a later
reader does not treat them alike:
sale_of_property/main         - retired. Correctly never joins. Permanent.
early_termination/placeholder - substitute text with no template paragraph of its own.
Permanent.
other_contingency/main        - NOT YET OBSERVED in any source. Expected to join once a
send using it appears. TEMPORARY, and nothing currently
prompts anyone to revisit it - the same stale-allowlist
risk rule 4 exists to catch, just deferred. Suggest a
`reason` field with a permanent/pending distinction.
